children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me: **How many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I have one child I'd like to ask about - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me here in the UK. I was wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to know about Alex, who is 8 years old and living with you in the UK.

To help me assess his eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask: **Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status/indefinite leave to remain in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen and I live here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Now I have a few more questions to complete the assessment.

**What is your current residency status? Are you living in the UK right now, and have you been living here continuously?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm living in the UK right now and have been living here continuously.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I have one more important question:

**Is Alex in full-time education or training, or does he have any disabilities or health conditions that might be relevant?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 8, so he's just in primary school - normal school for his age. Nothing special about education or training. He's been in hospital though - he's been there for about three months now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know that Alex has been in hospital for about three months. This is important information.

**Is Alex still currently in the hospital, or has he been discharged?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's still in the hospital at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. That's an important detail. Let me ask a clarifying question:

**While Alex is in the hospital, is he still living with you as his primary residence, or is the hospital now considered his place of residence?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he's in the hospital full-time right now - he's been there for the treatment. So I suppose the hospital is where he's staying at the moment, though of course he's still my son and this is his home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate you clarifying that. Let me ask one more important question to fully understand the situation:

**Are you receiving any support or allowance from the hospital or local authority specifically for Alex's care while he's in hospital - for example, things like free prescriptions, or support payments related to his hospital stay?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not receiving any support or payments from the hospital or local authority for his care while he's in there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all of that information. I now have enough details to assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit.

Based on what you've told me, let me explain the situation:

You are a British citizen living continuously in the UK, which meets the residency requirements. However, there is one key factor that affects Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit: **Alex is currently in hospital as his main place of residence**.

According to Child Benefit rules, a child must be living with you in your home to qualify. While Alex is your son and this is emotionally his home, the fact that he is currently in full-time hospital care and the hospital is his place of residence means he does not meet the residency requirement for Child Benefit at this time.

This situation may change if and when Alex is discharged from hospital and returns to live with you full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I hope this clarifies the situation. If you have any questions about this assessment, or if Alex's circumstances change, please do get in touch.
